rule.title: Strict Prohibition of Emojis in Production Interface Elements
rule.statement: Emojis must not be used as interface icons, status badges, buttons, or navigation indicators in production interfaces.
rule.rationale: Emojis render inconsistently across operating systems (Apple, Windows, Android), lack scalable vector styling, and cause screen readers to announce verbose, disruptive descriptions.
rule.implementation_guidance: Use curated SVG vector icons from Lucide React (<CheckIcon />, <AlertTriangleIcon />, <TrashIcon />).

source.evidence_quote: System icons should be cohesive, vector-based, and specifically designed for the interface context. Do not rely on platform emojis for core interface feedback.

rule.title: Jakob's Law: Conform to Familiar User Interface Mental Models
rule.statement: Users spend most of their time on other sites; interface layouts, navigation patterns, and iconography must conform to familiar mental models rather than inventing proprietary navigation mechanics.
rule.rationale: Violating conventional placement (e.g., placing the search bar in the bottom footer) causes cognitive friction and disorientation, driving user abandonment.
rule.implementation_guidance: Place primary navigation on the left sidebar or top header, search prominently in the top bar, and profile/settings in the top-right corner.

forbidden.example: Hiding the primary navigation inside an unlabelled floating action button at the bottom left.

preferred.example: Top navbar with Logo on left, Global Search centered, and User Avatar on right.

source.evidence_quote: Users spend most of their time on other sites. This means that users prefer your site to work the same way as all the other sites they already know.

rule.title: Hick's Law: Minimize Options to Reduce Decision Latency
rule.statement: Break down complex choices into distinct progressive steps; menus and selection dialogs should limit initial choices to high-frequency actions.
rule.rationale: Decision time increases logarithmically with the number and complexity of choices. Overwhelming users with 30 options causes choice paralysis.
rule.implementation_guidance: Highlight recommended presets. Move advanced esoteric settings into a secondary collapsible 'Advanced Settings' accordion.

forbidden.example: Presenting 25 unorganized sliders and dropdowns on the primary chat window.

preferred.example: Preset: Standard (8 Chunks), Detailed (12 Chunks). Advanced toggle: customize exact temperature and top-p.

source.evidence_quote: The time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices. Simplify choices for the user by breaking complex tasks into smaller steps.

rule.title: Miller's Law: Chunk Complex Information into 5 to 9 Discrete Units
rule.statement: Complex interfaces and forms must organize related information into discrete visual chunks containing no more than 7 (+/- 2) elements per group.
rule.rationale: Human working memory has an average capacity of 7 items. Cluttering an interface with unchunked data leads to cognitive overload and errors.
rule.implementation_guidance: Group document metadata into logical visual cards: Document Details, Indexing Metrics, Access Permissions.

forbidden.example: A single flat form page containing 28 continuous input fields without visual section headers.

preferred.example: Dividing a long onboarding form into 3 step-by-step wizard tabs, each containing 4 inputs.

source.evidence_quote: The average person can only keep 7 (plus or minus 2) items in their working memory. Organize content into smaller chunks to help users process and memorize easily.

rule.title: Perceived Performance via Skeleton Loaders (Doherty Threshold)
rule.statement: Content areas with predictable structure must render layout-matching Skeleton Shimmer loaders instead of spinning loaders during data retrieval.
rule.rationale: Skeleton screens reduce perceived loading latency by previewing the arriving content layout, satisfying the Doherty Threshold for user cognitive engagement.
rule.implementation_guidance: Render <Skeleton className='h-4 w-full' /> matching the typography and grid layout of arriving cards or tables.

forbidden.example: A centered spinning spinner icon in the middle of a blank white screen.

source.evidence_quote: Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures that neither has to wait on the other. Skeleton screens minimize perceived waiting time.
